questions.q: Why shouldn't RAG be treated as the default architecture for every LLM project?
options: RAG is illegal to use for commercial products
LLMs cannot technically support retrieval at all
It requires real, ongoing engineering work — chunking, embeddings, a vector database, retrieval tuning — that isn't worth it when a problem doesn't actually need it
RAG only works with one specific vendor's models
questions.explain: RAG adds meaningful infrastructure and maintenance; it pays off when a problem genuinely needs grounding in a large, changing knowledge base, and is wasted effort otherwise.

questions.q: If the information an LLM needs easily fits inside the prompt, what does this lesson recommend?
options: Split it into chunks and embed it regardless of size
Always fine-tune the model on it instead
Just include it directly in the prompt rather than building a retrieval pipeline for it
Build a vector database first, then evaluate whether it was needed
questions.explain: Standing up embeddings and a vector database for content that would fit directly in a prompt is unnecessary complexity for a problem that doesn't require it.

questions.q: If the real goal is changing the model's tone or writing style, why is RAG a poor fit?
options: Tone cannot be controlled by any method
RAG always makes the model's tone worse
Vector databases are incapable of storing text about tone
Style and tone are not knowledge-grounding problems — fine-tuning or clear prompt instructions address them more directly
questions.explain: Retrieval is about grounding answers in facts; changing how a model writes is a behavioral change better handled by fine-tuning or direct instructions, not by retrieving 'examples of tone.'

questions.q: Why is vector search a poor fit for a question like 'what's today's exchange rate'?
options: Vector search finds semantically similar text, not exact structured values — this needs a tool call or direct database/API query instead
Exchange rates never change, so no lookup is needed
Vector databases cannot store numbers
This type of question cannot be answered by any AI system
questions.explain: Similarity search surfaces text that resembles the query in meaning; an exact live value needs to be computed or looked up directly, not approximated through retrieval.

questions.q: According to this lesson's checklist, what signals that RAG is actually earning its complexity?
options: The knowledge base is tiny and never changes
The task is purely about matching a brand voice
The answer needs to be calculated rather than found in text
The knowledge exceeds what fits in a prompt, changes often, is fact-based, and needs to be found in text rather than computed
questions.explain: When most of the checklist questions come back 'yes' — too big for a prompt, changes often, about facts, found rather than computed — RAG is solving a real problem rather than adding unnecessary machinery.
